2.help:
The Same Criminal Episode
If you were convicted of ANY of the offenses in the same "Criminal Episode," answer YES to this question.

If the same case number was used, or the charges resulted from the same set of events or subject matter, they will typically be deemed to be part of the same Criminal Episode.

When you're arrested, it's frequently for more than one offense, even though some of those charges are dismissed or later dropped. In addition, it is not uncommon for prosecutors to file multiple charges as a tactic in negotiating plea bargains, eventually dismissing many of them.

Here is an example you may find helpful in understanding the concept:

If you were pulled over for driving while intoxicated, and the police found drugs in the car, these would be charges from the same arrest. If the drug charges were dismissed, but you were convicted of the driving while intoxicated charges, you would answer YES to this question. If both the driving while intoxicated charge and the drug charges were both dismissed, you would answer NO to this question.

4.help:
What is a Statute of Limitations?
A "Statute of Limitations" is the time allowed to file charges against you. The statute of limitations for some cases is as short as one year, while some serious criminal offenses have no limit and can be filed at any time, even decades after the crime occurred (an example would be murder). In Texas, most criminal offenses have statutes of limitation ranging from 2 to 10 years.

These time periods can vary quite a bit, so you often need to do a little research to find the right statute of limitation for your criminal offense. A good place to start here would be the Texas Code of Criminal Procedure Art. 12.01, et seq. However, here are some general time periods that should be helpful in answering this question:

Felonies With NO Statute of Limitations: Answer NO to this question if you were charged with any of the following crimes: Murder, Manslaughter, Sexual Assault, Human Trafficking, Compelling Prostitution of a Minor, Leaving the Scene of an Accident when a Death has Taken Place

Felonies With 10 Year Statutes of Limitations: Answer NO to this question if it has not yet been 10 years since one of these criminal events occurred. Examples of these types of felonies would be: Compelling Prostitution, Arson, Crimes Involving Injury to the Elderly or Disabled, Forgery, and Theft offenses by government employees.

Felonies with 7 Year Statutes of Limitations: Answer NO to this question if it has not yet been 7 years since one of these criminal events occurred. Examples of these types of felonies include: Identity Theft, Money Laundering, Fraud, Bigamy, and certain financial and tax crimes.

Felonies with 5 Year Statutes of Limitations: Answer NO to this question of it has not yet been 5 years since one of these criminal events occurred. Examples of these types of felonies would be: Insurance Fraud, many Theft offenses, Robbery, Burglary, and Endangering or Abandoning a Child.

All Other Felonies Have a 3 Year Statute of Limitations: Answer NO to this question if it has not yet been 3 years since one of these criminal events has occurred.

Most Misdemeanors have a 2 Year Statute of Limitation: Answer NO to this question if it has not yet been 2 years since one of these criminal events has occurred.

6.question: Were your charges dismissed for "Lack of Probable Cause"? If you're not sure, please click the help button.
6.help:
What is "Lack of Probable Cause"?

Answer YES if your case was dismissed for Lack of Probable Cause.

"Lack of probable cause": This means that your case was dismissed because the evidence proved that you did not commit the offense.

Examples:
  • Your case for sexual assault was dismissed because the alleged victim stated that he/she was lying, or DNA proved it was not you.
  • Your case for domestic violence was dismissed because the alleged victim stated that he/she was not actually assaulted and lied to police.
  • Lack of Probable Cause is NOT a case being dismissed because the victim failed to testify, or the Officer failed to testify.

answers.value: Yes, my charges were dismissed for lack of probable cause

14.question: Were you put on deferred for prostitution or any of the crimes listed in the help button?
14.help:
Obscenity-Related Offenses

Answer YES to this question if you were put on deferred adjudication for or convicted of a violation of Texas Penal Code Chapter 43, which covers Prostitution and Obscenity-Related Offenses.

The offenses in this chapter are Prostitution and Obscenity-Related Offenses, some of which are felonies. The following is a list of criminal offenses listed in Chapter 43:

  • Prostitution
  • Promotion of Prostitution (all types)
  • Compelling Prostitution
  • Obscene Display or Distribution
  • Obscenity
  • Sale, Distribution, Display of Harmful Material to a Minor
  • Sexual Performance by a Child
  • Employment Harmful to Children and
  • Child Pornography Crimes
